chapter: Publishing, Jelly Roll in Los Angeles and band lore
title: Les Hite and how Lionel Hampton came to Los Angeles
summary: Curtis Mosby was a drummer, not a violinist. Saxophonist Les Hite persuaded Spikes to send for the young drummer Lionel Hampton, who worked in the band two or three years until he joined Benny Goodman.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Uh, no, there were a few more things I wanted to ask you about. Uh, one of... They mention here...uh, in this issue of
Storyville that some discographies list uh, Curtis Mosby as playing violin. He didn't play violin, did he?
That's what I thought--but he didn't also play violin?
And some of the musicians that uh, were around then--I just wonder if you remember anything about, like, for instance, Les Hite--he played in your band, didn't he?

Les Hite played in my band, yeah. Les Hite was my saxophone player, and he...he's the cause of me getting Lionel 'cause when he left New York...uh, Chicago, I mean, he was playing with Lionel around there. Little school band, like, you know. When Les come out here, it was the first trip he made. He come out here with...uh...uh... some singer that had five pieces and [they were] on the Orpheum, [circuit] and when they got here, Les quit, and the other boy quit. There was two ...three of 'em quit, and I had both of 'em in...er, tenor and alto, and the other boy went back home, and Les stayed out here, and then he told me about Lionel, so I sent and got Lionel.
Because you showed me that clipping where Lionel credited you with giving him his start in the band business.

Yeah. Well, you see, Lionel was only about eighteen, nineteen years old, and Les Hite told me what a drummer--what a good drummer he was and everything. I don't think Les Hite was over twenty-two or twenty-three, and so he told me...persuaded me to send and
get Lionel, and I sent and got Lionel.
And then Lionel worked for you in your band or...
Until he went with Benny Goodman. Two, three years. A coupla years, I think it was.
Ohhhh. Didn't he also work with the Black and Tan?
No. No, No, he never worked with the Black and Tan. Paul Whiteman...er, Paul Howard was with Black and Tan, you know.
Yeah. I thought they worked together at some point.
